newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan court jails 25 students to three months.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan court jails 25 students to three months.

text.p: A Moroccan court sentenced 25 Moslem fundamentalist students on Monday to three months in jail after it found them guilty of disturbing public order and damaging a state-owned property, a court official said.
The Casablanca-based court also fined them 2,500 dirhams ($275) each, he said. All 25 defendants pleaded not guilty.
The court is expected to hand down a verdict on Tuesday in another trial involving three other students on similar charges.

The students were arrested more than two weeks ago after protests on a university campus to press demands for the improvement of their material conditions, including transportation, a student union spokesman had said.
Police say the students belong to the outlawed Islamic Al-Adl-Wal Ihsane (Justice and Charity) group, led by Sheikh Yassine who is now in his seventh year under house arrest.

The group was found as a charity association in 1980. It applied for official recognition as a political party a year later but the Interior Ministry rejected the demand. The association was banned in 1990.
